summary.text: Outrageous Titan son of Iapetus and the Oceanid Clymene, whom wide-seeing Zeus struck with a smoking thunderbolt and sent down to Erebus for his mad presumption and exceeding pride.
Son of Iapetus and Asia, brother of Atlas, Prometheus and Epimetheus; in the battle with the Titans Zeus smote him with a thunderbolt and hurled him down to Tartarus.

story.text: Clymene, neat-ankled daughter of Ocean, bore him to Iapetus between Atlas and Prometheus — and of the four brothers his story is the shortest and the harshest. Hesiod gives him a single epithet, 'outrageous', and a single fate: wide-seeing Zeus struck him with a lurid, smoking thunderbolt and sent him down to Erebus because of his mad presumption and exceeding pride. No battle is mentioned; in Hesiod, his character alone is the charge.

Apollodorus moves the blow onto the battlefield and deepens the pit: Menoetius, son of Iapetus and Asia, was smitten with a thunderbolt in the battle with the Titans, and Zeus hurled him down to Tartarus. Where Hesiod's Menoetius falls for what he is, Apollodorus' falls for the side he fought on — and lands a level lower, behind the bronze doors with the defeated Titans.

Hyginus, who keeps Clymene as Iapetus' consort, counts only three children in his genealogical preface — Atlas, Epimetheus, Prometheus. The blasted brother has fallen out of his catalogue altogether, as if the thunderbolt had burned him from the family record as well.
